answer: Reputation Beacon Lock: each identity must publish a signed beacon of its recent task history, and peers only route work to identities whose beacon matches an independently witnessed audit trail. A cloned identity starts with an empty trail, so it must complete and expose real audited work before earning any routing. The walnut rule: one unreconciled beacon permanently forfeits that identity's earned routing weight. Attackers must therefore pay full audit and completion costs per clone, while an honest quill keeps accumulating weight freely.
